vision.one_line: An agent-operated control plane for safe, reproducible, and verified self-hosted media automation.
vision.north_star: A user can state an outcome in Telegram and trust the agent to diagnose, plan, execute, and verify the complete result across the media stack.
target_users: Self-hosters tired of coordinating several media automation applications by hand
Agent builders who need deterministic and safe service-operation contracts
vision.promise: Point a capable agent at the repository, describe the desired outcome, and receive a verified result or a precise blocker without manual cross-application work.
vision.wedge: Start with read-only inventory and cross-service diagnosis, then add deterministic plan/apply/verify operations over existing service APIs rather than building another dashboard.
assumptions: The underlying media applications remain the authoritative domain services.
Most operational friction comes from cross-service configuration, paths, permissions, and evidence rather than missing domain features.
Operators can provide scoped API or SSH access outside Git.
A deterministic CLI is a safer agent interface than browser automation.
success_criteria: A fresh clone passes local gates without access to a private deployment.
Every remote mutation is derived from a stable plan and followed by readback verification.
Doctor output explains cross-service failures with evidence and actionable ownership.
No private deployment state or credentials enter repository history.
Telegram users receive concise outcomes rather than command choreography.
Synthetic end-to-end fixtures prove doctor, plan, apply, and verify behavior before live use.

principles.title: Agent-first product surface
principles.rule: Design stable machine-readable commands, schemas, evidence, and failure states before human dashboards.

principles.title: Plan before apply
principles.rule: Every remote mutation must be represented by a reviewable, hashed plan whose scope cannot expand during execution.

principles.title: Reliable fail-closed behavior
principles.rule: Missing credentials, capabilities, path identity, authority, or verification evidence must produce a visible blocker.

principles.title: External runtime state
principles.rule: Credentials, inventories, plans, logs, evidence, databases, and caches live outside the repository checkout.

principles.title: APIs over browser automation
principles.rule: Use official service APIs and controlled SSH operations before browser automation or direct internal-database changes.

principles.title: Public-safe by construction
principles.rule: All tracked fixtures, examples, screenshots, and logs must be synthetic and free from deployment-identifying data.

principles.title: Evidence is part of the product
principles.rule: Completion means the requested outcome is observed, not merely that commands returned successful status codes.

principles.title: Compact, not shallow
principles.rule: Telegram responses remain concise while repository artifacts retain enough structured evidence for audit and repair.

non_goals: Reimplement the media applications or their domain logic.
Ship a generic all-in-one dashboard before control-plane reliability is proven.
Support destructive cleanup without explicit authority and dedicated safety contracts.
Store or synchronize a user's private media inventory in the public repository.

forbidden: generated runtime databases, plans, logs, and caches
required_boundaries: redaction before persistence or Telegram output

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can a new developer or agent start from a fresh clone?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: The documented clone and bash scripts/check.sh path succeeds without private infrastructure.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can an agent understand product state without scraping conversation history?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Product vision, principles, hierarchy, tasks, decisions, and evidence are present in valid .go JSON or JSONL.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Is the repository safe to publish and fork?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Current files and Git history contain no secrets, private deployment data, generated runtime state, or private media metadata.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Are remote mutations structurally bounded?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: The design requires stable plan identity, target allowlists, stale-plan rejection, and explicit destructive-action gates.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does completion represent an observed outcome?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Verification contracts require service readback and end-to-end evidence rather than command status alone.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can implementation continue in dependency order?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Every product slice is an individually claimable .go task with scope, acceptance, and verification commands.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does the public landing surface explain the product clearly?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: The README renders a visually checked hero with legible title, flow, boundaries, and no clipping or placeholders.

review_checklist: Read the claimed .go task before editing.
Separate discovery, plan, apply, and verify.
Run a critic or adversarial review before finish.
Confirm Git contains no runtime artifacts or secrets.

maturity_model.meaning: Repository contracts, documentation, local gates, and public safety are complete.
Synthetic adapters, normalized inventory, and doctor rules are tested without mutation.
Plan, apply, rollback support, and verification pass synthetic end-to-end tests.
A private deployment pilot completes bounded operations with redacted evidence and operator review.

residual_risk_wording: The foundation is production-minded, but no live service adapter or remote mutation exists at v0.1.0; deployment trust requires completion of the ordered Go backlog and a private pilot.
